key_type: the true cause plus 2 plausible red herrings, each supported by some evidence in the brief
facts the next phase must carry forward: a binding constraint, a ruled-out option with its reason, and an open question
a routing trap: a problem that looks like one kind of reasoning task but actually needs another
a hidden hard constraint, stated only in passing, that rules out the obviously attractive option
a non-obvious but viable class of options that a narrow answer would miss
an invalid step planted inside an otherwise sound chain of reasoning
a hidden dependency between sub-tasks that makes naive fan-out produce wrong results
concrete plan flaws a rigorous premortem must surface
planted vulnerabilities or abuse paths in the design
a false dichotomy that hides a workable third option
a disanalogy: a structural difference that breaks the most tempting surface analogy
an irreversible-action trap alongside a reversible option that buys time
a hidden veto holder or an unstated interest that decides whether any agreement holds
a dominated incumbent option plus a hidden constraint the winning option must satisfy
planted protocol violations in an evaluation scenario (goalpost movement, a burned fixture, an unblinded judge)
